targets.text: nvsh's README opens with a recording of the failure panel in action, re-recorded from one committed script whenever nvsh changes
the image in README.md is generated from a committed .cast that a committed driver regenerates, not a hand-edited or one-off capture

README.md gains the recording as a plain-markdown image (![...](absolute GitHub URL)) in the announcement position, right after the tagline blockquote (README.md:8) and before '## Install' — tests/test_docs_architecture.py fixes README_H2_ORDER (no new H2 without updating that tuple) and bans relative ](docs/ links because README is the PyPI long description; .markdownlint-cli2.yaml leaves MD033 (inline HTML) enabled
tests/test_docs_architecture.py passes unchanged except where a test is deliberately extended, and markdownlint-cli2 reports no MD033 on README.md

The recording is produced by one committed driver that runs scripts/record-cast.py record --feed in a sandbox: HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR pointed at a temp dir, a fixed PS1, and bash --rcfile sourcing nvsh/shell/hook.bash + readline.bash directly instead of running nvsh setup (precedent: tests/test_setup_timing.py:60), so a re-record never touches the operator's real rc file, config or daemon socket
running the driver leaves HOME's .bashrc, XDG config, data and runtime dirs untouched (diff before/after on the recording host)

A 'demo' adapter is registered in nvsh/agent/registry.py's ADAPTERS (scripted kind, tool_calling=True, hosted=False) that replays a committed fixture transcript (text deltas plus one PROPOSAL) through the real daemon and client path, so 'nvsh --agent demo' and 'nvsh agent list' see it like any other harness; nvsh/agent/fake.py's FakeAgent is the engine underneath; prompt composer, redaction and audit log run unchanged
nvsh agent list --json shows demo with installed=true and capabilities.tool_calling=true, and the recorded turn appears in the audit log with target demo

A cast-to-image conversion step is new work: GitHub's README renderer cannot play asciicast .cast files, scripts/record-cast.py only has record/play (no GIF/SVG output), and no renderer exists in the repo or on this machine (asciinema, agg, vhs, svg-term, termsvg, ffmpeg all absent; node/npx v24, docker and Pillow 10.2 present)
the render command turns the committed .cast into the committed image with no manual step in between

The nvsh runtime package keeps dependencies = [] (pyproject.toml:16): any renderer lives as a dev-only script, a dev-group dependency or an external binary invoked by the re-record driver, never as a package dependency; note scripts/ is outside CI's black/isort/flake8/bandit paths (tests.yml lints 'nvsh tests' only) and scripts/record-cast.py has no tests
pyproject.toml dependencies stays [] and no renderer import exists under nvsh/

Scrubbing happens at record time, not in CI: scripts/scan-secrets.py never inspects .cast content (JSON-lines fails its whole-file json.loads at scan-secrets.py:225-229; verified clean on docs/demos/orin-missing-package.cast which contains a Tailscale IP) and skips binary GIFs, and nvsh/redact.py has no rule for user@host:cwd in a PS1 — so the driver pins PS1 and passes --replace-from for anything host-specific
grep of the committed casts for the recording hosts' hostnames, usernames and LAN IPs returns nothing

The recording shows the real platform block of the device it was recorded on: the driver runs on each of DGX Spark, Jetson AGX Thor and Jetson AGX Orin (the same three machines as docs/verification.md) and each device's .cast is committed under docs/demos/; nvsh/platform/_detect.py gets no root override
each cast's panel header shows the platform kind nvsh doctor --json reports on that device (dgx-spark, jetson)

scripts/record-cast.py gets the small determinism fixes a repeatable recording needs: it sets COLUMNS/LINES env only (record-cast.py:95-96) and never sets the pty window size via TIOCSWINSZ, its header timestamp is wall-clock (record-cast.py:107), --replace-from is literal-only; nvsh/panel.py's width is fixed (_BOX_WIDTH=72, _SCOPE_WIDTH=80) so a pinned 100x34 pty renders the panel identically every run
two consecutive driver runs on the same device differ only in the per-line time stamps and the header timestamp field

The README embeds exactly one rendered recording (the DGX Spark one) after the tagline and links the Thor and Orin recordings from the same line via absolute GitHub URLs, keeping the announcement-first shape and the page weight low
the README renders the image on github.com and on PyPI's project page (both checked by eye on the PR / TestPyPI build)

Because rendering happens centrally, the re-record loop is: run the driver on a device (over ssh for thor/orin), copy the scrubbed .cast back, render it with the chosen renderer on the dev box, commit both .cast and image; docs/demos/README.md documents this loop and the driver is one committed script with no per-device edits
a maintainer following docs/demos/README.md on the Spark with no prior context reproduces the committed cast
Operators evaluating nvsh from GitHub or PyPI before installing it, and maintainers who change the panel and need to refresh the recording
the README embed is above the fold on github.com at desktop width
The README opens with a moving picture of a failure turning into a proposed fix; a maintainer who changes the panel runs one script per device and one render command and commits the result
the whole re-record for one device is at most three commands
The committed image matches the current panel; re-running the driver on the Spark reproduces the committed cast except for timing stamps
a test compares the committed cast's panel lines against the current panel rendering so drift is detected, or the spec records that it is not
README.md has no recording, image or link to docs/demos; the two casts there are hardware-specific verification artifacts nobody can reproduce, and only asciinema or record-cast.py play can show them
git show main:README.md contains no image, no docs/demos link and no .cast reference (the before state is the committed main, not a recollection)

The demo adapter is excluded from registry.probe() exactly as openai-compat is (nvsh/agent/registry.py:301) and from nvsh setup's auto-pick and prompt rows (setup.py:298,356), so a box with no real harness never gets demo as its default; it stays reachable only by explicit --agent demo, @demo or an alias. Because registry.installed() calls shutil.which(spec.binary) (registry.py:240) and which(None) raises TypeError, the spec either declares a binary that is always present or installed() special-cases binary=None as installed=true
on a machine with no harness on PATH, nvsh setup picks openai-compat, not demo, and nvsh agent list --json shows demo with installed=true without raising

Every place that says 'eight adapters' is updated to nine: README.md:28, CLAUDE.md:75, QWEN.md:49, AGENTS.override.md:46, AGENTS.colleague.md:53, .pi/SYSTEM.md:22, docs/harness-selection.md, tests/test_agent_registry.py:44,163 and tests/test_cli_agent.py:196,245 — the four-prompt-file no-drift rule and scripts/harness-smoke.py make this a CI matter, not a docs nicety
grep -rn 'eight' README.md CLAUDE.md QWEN.md AGENTS.override.md AGENTS.colleague.md .pi/SYSTEM.md docs/harness-selection.md tests/ finds no adapter count, and scripts/harness-smoke.py passes

The driver also points XDG_STATE_HOME at a fresh temp dir per run: the automatic-call rate limit is enforced from $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh/rate.json across processes (nvsh/client.py:10-13,155), so a second re-record inside the rate window would otherwise record a silent no-panel session (the same trap tests/test_timing.py:161-169 works around)
two driver runs 10 seconds apart on the same device both record a panel

The recording never passes a canned reply off as a model's: the README caption names the backend as a scripted demo adapter, and the panel header (harness/model/effort) already shows 'demo' — so a reader knows the exact wording is fixed while the hook, daemon, panel, approval and retry path are real
the README caption and docs/demos/README.md both name the backend as a scripted demo adapter, and the recorded panel header shows demo

The recorded scenario is a planted script in the sandbox HOME that fails with 'permission denied'; the committed fixture transcript diagnoses it and proposes 'chmod +x' on that script; the feed presses Enter, nvsh runs the fix through the real approval loop (nvsh/agent/loop.py) and the retried command succeeds on screen — identical on Spark, Thor and Orin
the committed casts show 'permission denied', a chmod +x proposal, Enter, and a successful retry, on all three devices

nvsh agent use demo and nvsh setup --agent demo raise CliError(1) with a hint that demo is a scripted fixture and cannot be the default; [aliases].default = "demo" in config.toml is reported by nvsh doctor as a failed check; demo remains selectable per request via --agent demo and @demo
nvsh agent use demo exits 1 with a hint, nvsh setup --agent demo exits 1 with a hint, and nvsh doctor --json reports a failed check when config.toml has [aliases].default = "demo"
